source_evidence.observation: [E4] The requested conclusion is that the function's finite-value domain is confined to a bounded neighborhood of λ = 0, rather than extending over all real λ.

binders: [E2, E3] A real-valued random variable X.
[E3, E4] A real parameter λ varying over the domain of the displayed function.
hypotheses: [E2] X ∼ N(0, 1), i.e. X is standard normal.
conclusions: [E3, E4] The set of real λ for which E exp(λ²X²) is finite is a bounded neighborhood of 0; in particular, this expectation is not finite for every real λ.

[E3, E4] Mathematical unpacking of the standard-normal integral gives the maximal finiteness domain |λ| < 1/√2 (equivalently λ² < 1/2); at and beyond the boundary |λ| = 1/√2 the nonnegative expectation diverges. This exact threshold is an analyst derivation that resolves the qualitative source wording, not a threshold printed in the exercise.
definitions_and_conventions: [E2] N(0, 1) denotes the standard normal law (mean 0 and variance 1).
[E3] exp(λ²X²) is formed pointwise from the square of the real parameter and the square of X, and E denotes expectation.
[E4] ‘Finite’ concerns whether the nonnegative expectation has a finite real value, as opposed to the extended value +∞.
[E4] A bounded neighborhood of zero contains an open interval about 0 and is bounded as a subset of ℝ.
implicit_context: [E2, E3] X is defined on an implicit probability space and expectation is taken with respect to its probability law.
[E1] Only part (a) of Exercise 2.5.5 is selected; part (b), which assumes a global bound involving a constant K, is a separate claim and contributes no hypothesis here.

semantic_facets.topic: exact maximal domain derived from the selected claim
details: [E2, E3, E4] Using the standard-normal density, the integrand times the density is proportional to exp(-(1/2-λ²)x²), so integrability holds exactly when λ² < 1/2.
[E2, E3, E4] Thus the maximal finiteness neighborhood is (-1/√2, 1/√2), and both endpoints are excluded; this calculation is analyst inference rather than an explicit formula in the source text.

contract_plain_english: For a standard normal random variable X, study the real-parameter square-exponential moment λ ↦ E[exp(λ²X²)]. The source asks one to show that this expectation is finite only near λ = 0, on a bounded neighborhood rather than for all real λ. Computing against the standard-normal density gives the exact maximal neighborhood (-1/√2, 1/√2): the expectation is finite there and diverges at both endpoints and beyond. The exact radius is a mathematical resolution of the source's qualitative phrase, not a number printed in the exercise.
